I will keep the farm simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the most practical pattern for me is still winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am 65, so I will not spread myself across too many crops that need more labor, more marketing, or more technical management. Wheat and maize are the crops I know best, the machinery is easy to arrange, the inputs are familiar, and the risk is easier for me to control.

At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already the main crop in the field, so I will manage it carefully through spring water and fertilizer, then harvest it in early summer. After that, I will sow summer maize right away to catch the season. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, because I want stable yield more than experimentation. I will use moderate fertilizer rather than chasing the highest yield, because I care more about avoiding waste and keeping costs under control. I will irrigate only at the key stages, since water matters but too much water is unnecessary. For pests and diseases, I will spray only as needed at the usual local control windows. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage and fits my usual way of farming.
